------------------------------------------------------------------------

We invited a family—and the brother’s family—for lunch. We knew only the basics about them: they studied Computer Science, and they came from the storied land once called the *Golden Bird*—*Aryavarta (आर्यावर्त)*. Beyond that, despite seeing them for over a year, hearing their church talks, and knowing a bit about his journey to Christianity, our conversations rarely moved beyond warm greetings and brief exchanges.

A few weeks ago, however, something changed.

He spoke about the hymn **“How Firm a Foundation,”** especially the third verse—one that had also been on my mind:

> *Fear not, I am with thee; oh, be not dismayed,*\
>
> *For I am thy God and will still give thee aid.*\
>
> *I’ll strengthen thee, help thee, and cause thee to stand,*\
>
> *Upheld by my righteous, omnipotent hand.*

Hearing him speak about that verse—with conviction and tenderness—felt like an invitation to know them better. So we took the next step.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Eight visitors arrived that afternoon.\

Two families, each with two children—the older a daughter, the younger a son.\

One family lived in Richfield, the other studied Computer Science at BYU.

Our conversation ranged wide and warm.

We talked about **arranged marriages**, **family traditions**, and **the beauty of multilingual life**.\

Arranged or family involved, initiated marriages are still widely practiced—and often preferred—tradition.

Mentioned how someone from Hong Kong once said that arranged marriage works precisely because expectations start low and naturally grow better over time. Dating, on the other hand, often begins with *high* expectations and often drop over time.

Telugu, we learned, is the **4th most spoken language in India**, with **70+ million speakers**—about as many as Korean and Cantonese combined. He himself grew up speaking **Telugu, Hindi, and English**, and fully expected his children to do the same.

He shared how his childhood faith emphasized **fear and justice**, but discovering Christianity revealed a God of **love and mercy**.\

He explained **cricket** to someone who only knew **baseball**, and with a shy smile admitted that he once dreamed of becoming a cricket star.

When they finally put on their shoes and stepped out into the rainy afternoon, something unexpected lingered.

It felt not simply like guests had left my home—\

but as if *I* had briefly visited a home somewhere in the warm, green southeastern provinces of India, carried there by their stories, their laughter, and their generosity of spirit.
